mappings.note: Who wrote the lesson -- knowing the text one has read, not a detail inside it, so the read-with-comprehension LO rather than LO-92.
Where Jody let his thoughts drift back to -- a point stated in the story.
Whom he spoke to first -- character detail.
Why his father is proud of him -- a reason given in the narrative.
Completing 'the fawn may be out there yet. It might be ___' -- recall of a stated line.
What 'hemmed in' means -- inferring an unfamiliar phrase from context, the vocabulary LO rather than a plot detail.
Completing 'surely it seems ___ to leave it to starve' -- recall of a stated line.
What his mother was doing -- stated detail.
Who said 'nothing in the world comes quite free' -- attributing a line to a character, so LO-92; LO-93 would apply if the question asked what the saying means.
Who offered Jody a ride -- character detail.
How Jody knew it was a boy -- a reason given in the narrative.
Whether Jody wanted company -- stated detail.
Why Mill-wheel would not leave him alone -- a reason given in the narrative.
What acted as a compass in the forest -- stated detail.
Whether Jody thought he had lost his direction -- stated detail.
How he got rid of the buzzards -- sequence of events.
Whose footprints the sand showed -- stated detail.
Why the buzzards clacked their wings -- a reason given in the narrative.
Whether the fawn tried to rise or run -- stated detail.
What 'delirious' means in the quoted line -- inferring an unfamiliar word from context.
Completing 'as gently as though the fawn were ___' -- recall of a stated line.
What the fawn smelt of -- stated detail.
Why Jody's heart thumped -- a reason given in the narrative.
What 'light-headed' means -- inferring an unfamiliar word from context.
Who told Jody 'a fawn will follow if it had first been carried' -- attributing a line to a character.
Which month it was -- stated detail.
How the fawn got up the steps -- sequence of events.
Completing 'the boy's eyes were as ___ as the fawn's' -- recall of a stated line.
How Penny felt on seeing the fawn -- character detail.
Completing 'it was ___ to feel its tongue against his hand' -- recall of a stated line.
'I ___ as a President by the community' -- passive voice, which LO-98 names; LO-99 covers grammar games, not drills.
'The keys ___ without permission' -- passive voice.
'The matter ___ into by the relevant authority now' -- passive of a prepositional verb.
'A notorious thief ___ by the police' -- passive voice.
'I ___ waiting at the bank by my friend' -- passive voice.
'The criminal ___ by the police' -- passive voice.
'Short-listed candidates ___ for an interview next week' -- future passive.
'Years ago, butter ___ by hand' -- past passive.
'All the work ___ before Varun arrived' -- past perfect passive.
'In the olden days, grains ___ by the roller mill' -- past passive.
'His return ___ by us' -- passive voice.
'The sight ___ us with happiness' -- active/passive pairing, grammar.
'I ___ much ___ by his voice and manner' -- passive voice.
'His voice and manner ___ me' -- the active counterpart, grammar.
'Dr. Jai ___ in the nurse' -- verb form, grammar.
